name: Cross-sectional funding dispersion — long leg (low-funding perps, carry received)
rationale: Funding-rate dispersion edge: among the 20-asset OKX USDT-M perp universe, perpetuals whose funding sits in the BOTTOM quartile of the cross-sectional distribution represent the 'cheapest-to-hold-long' or 'most-pessimistic' assets — longs in these perps pay little or no carry, and in a negative-funding environment actually RECEIVE carry. The xsec_funding_rank feature is a per-bar cross-sectional percentile rank of the funding rate across the screened OKX universe [0=lowest, 1=highest]. Long-leg entry: rank below a fitted ceiling (bottom quartile). Paired with the short-high-funding leg (xsec-funding-dispersion-short-leg.json), the two legs form a dollar-neutral book: market beta cancels, the residual is the funding-dispersion premium. Leverage: 2:1 gross exposure (FR-legal; ESMA/MiCA retail cap at OKX EU). Funding accrues to P&L every bar via funding_feature — a long pays funding when rate is positive, receives it when negative. Exit when rank normalises back past a fitted mid-point (the premium has closed) or the stop fires. Vol ceiling keeps us out of crash/whipsaw regimes where the premium inverts. No magic numbers.
catalyst: Cross-sectional funding dispersion: low-funding perps are under-crowded relative to the universe; long collects the carry advantage or pays less carry than peers.
